answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: Within 15 minutes. The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes at 1-800-746-1553 once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred. A death of an individual at the mine is one of the listed accidents.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately, without delay, and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number once the operator knows or should know an accident has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is a covered accident.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. The 0.4 percent increase per 0.1 percent of methane applies only where methane is present, so it doesn't apply here.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The increase of 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane applies only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator must make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. The training must be conducted in conditions that duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable. About 8 of the 40 hours are given at the minesite.

claims.text: A new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training must duplicate actual underground conditions as closely as practicable, and approximately 8 hours are given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, which is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This appears in both 30 CFR 57.9300 (underground metal and nonmetal mines) and 56.9300 (surface metal and nonmetal mines).

claims.text: Under 57.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Under 56.9300, the same height requirement applies.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. Under 30 CFR 7.506(b)(1), mechanisms and procedures must be provided so that the breathable air within the refuge alternative does this.

claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not address OSHA bloodborne pathogens exposure control plans. They cover only MSHA regulations on respiratory protection and respirable dust control plans.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system. They cover mine slopes, shafts and buckets under MSHA rules, not OSHA trenching.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design information and permits for mining under bodies of water, which are different topics.
